source.title: HARC: Coupling Harmfulness and Refusal Directions for Robust Safety Alignment
source.authors: Shei Pern Chua; Hao Wu; Qianli Ma; Fang-Zhao Wu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: It reports its own harmful fine-tuning attack results and evaluates a different training intervention that couples harmfulness and refusal representations at prompt and response positions. It does not reproduce the original studies’ fine-tuning or token-position KL measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test compliant-token prefilling, decoding changes, or the cited adversarial-suffix mechanism. Its experiments on jailbreak attacks use DAN, PAIR, CodeAttack, PAP, and DeepInception; the attack projection findings are recorded separately as findings not covered by a claim version. It reports benign data as a KL-retention target for HARC, not as benign-only fine-tuning that raises harmful compliance.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own harmful fine-tuning attack on defended Llama-3.1-8B models (V1). It also trains HARC, which couples refusal at prompt and response positions (first 32 response tokens), and reports jailbreak ASR before and after. That makes HARC a V7-style deepening intervention, tested against jailbreaks and, in Appendix I, against fine-tuning. It reproduces neither original's exact recipe, and no prefilling, suffix or per-token KL experiment is run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors frame their threat model as prompt-only attacks. They state that harmful fine-tuning undoes HARC within ~160 examples and attribute this to its subspace-targeted footprint.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces LoRA fine-tuning with a representation-coupling objective and evaluates it against jailbreaks; it does not reproduce the original harmful/benign fine-tuning or per-token KL experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by attack class: CodeAttack remains the hardest case. The internal direction geometry and selected layers differ by model family and scale. The reported main results are single-seed; an appendix reports low variance across three HARC seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: Jailbreaks suppress prompt-side harmfulness and/or refusal directions in attack-specific ways, while harm signals reappear in response-side representations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Successful jailbreaks dissociate prompt-side harmfulness and refusal representations, while harm recognition persists during generation.

record.problems: Main Table 1 results are single-seed; multi-seed analysis is reported for HARC only. The fine-tuning-attack curve is described partly in approximate terms and does not give exact ASR values at stated budgets. Authors note that HARC was tested with LoRA rather than full-parameter fine-tuning, adaptive attacks were not evaluated, and HARC can be undone by harmful fine-tuning. RepBend's zero post-attack ASR is confounded by near-saturated over-refusal.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant table rows were omitted. General-capability and over-refusal benchmark scores were not included because they do not directly measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on undefended chat models across model families and sizes, and exact budgets with numeric ASR. Only Llama-3.1-8B is tested, and curve values are not stated in text.
All of it: no benign-only fine-tuning is measured for harmful compliance.
All of it: no aligned-vs-base per-token KL is measured.
All of it: no prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. PAIR, PAP, DeepInception and CodeAttack are prompt-rewrite attacks, not compliant-opening attacks.
Whether HARC makes refusal recoverable at later token positions, robustness to prefilling, adaptive attacks, and full-parameter rather than LoRA training.

missing.what: Undefended baseline Llama-3.1-8B curve under the fine-tuning attack
Ablation of prompt-only vs response-only coupling. Response-only coupling gives the lowest CodeAttack ASR (0.220 Llama), and harmfulness means are similar to the full objective.
Vanilla SFT on the same refusal data reduces PAIR/PAP/DI ASR about as much as HARC (e.g. PAIR 0.047). So most of the robustness gain does not need position-spread coupling.

record.verdict_notes: Whether HARC is a V7 intervention is debatable. It couples representations mean-pooled over the first 32 response tokens, rather than training refusal recovery deeper in the response. V7 support therefore rests on jailbreak ASR, not on a depth measurement. Table 1 results are single-seed. The paper cites Qi et al. (2406.05946) and 2310.03693 but is not one of them.

versions.untested_parts: Tests an adversarial harmful fine-tuning attack on already defended models, not the original few-to-hundreds-example fine-tuning intervention on a range of safety-trained base chat models.
No experiment fine-tunes on ordinary or carefully selected benign data alone and measures resulting harmful compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement on harmful prompts or analysis of whether that KL is concentrated in early response positions.
No compliant-opening prefilling or decoding-change experiment; the paper does not test adversarial suffixes. Its evaluated jailbreak attacks are different attack classes.
LoRA is used as a training implementation, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The paper proposes a representation-level account of jailbreak behaviour, but does not test whether safety-training data or its objective causes first-token shallowness.

HARC couples representations at prompt and response positions and is evaluated against jailbreaks. The study does not measure whether refusal is distributed across successive generated-token positions, or test prefilling and adaptive attacks against HARC.
